previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, diabetes, and recent hernia repair was admitted for evaluation of fevers and chills at home. He was found to have hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease, likely prerenal in origin due to reduced intake during illness. He was treated with kayexalate and IV fluids, with improvement in potassium and renal function. Infectious workup was negative, including normal chest X-ray, negative C. diff toxin, and no growth in urine culture; blood cultures later identified Enterobacter cloacae complex but were interpreted in the context of likely contamination. The fever resolved without antibiotics, presumed viral. Tacrolimus was discontinued and sirolimus increased to 4 mg daily given therapeutic levels and concern for tacrolimus-related nephrotoxicity. Lasix was held during admission. The patient was discharged home afebrile with follow-up arranged in the transplant clinic and instructions to monitor sirolimus levels.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male post-liver transplant in ___ with positive
blood cultures.  Evaluation for pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___

PA AND LATERAL CHEST RADIOGRAPHS:  The lungs are clear.  There is no focal
consolidation or pneumothorax.  There is no vascular congestion or pleural
effusions.  Cardiomediastinal and hilar contours are within normal limits.  A
biliary stent is noted in the right upper quadrant.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process

INDICATION:  ___ man status post liver transplant in ___ and
hernia repair one month ago.  Admitted with Gram-negative rod bacteremia. 
Evaluate for abscess and fluid collection.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were obtained from the lung bases to the pubic
symphysis.  P.o. contrast was administered.  Axial images were interpreted in
conjunction with coronal and sagittal reformats.

DLP:  418 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

CT ABDOMEN:

The visualized lung base and visualized heart are unremarkable.  No pleural or
pericardial effusion.

Intraabdominal evaluation is limited by lack of IV contrast.  The patient is
status post liver transplant.  Biliary stents are unchanged in position and
previously described pneumobilia is essentially stable.  No definite new focal
hepatic lesion.  The spleen is unremarkable.  The pancreas is atrophied and
unchanged.  The visualized esophagus and stomach are normal.  The small bowel
and colon have a normal course and caliber with contrast reaching the rectum.

No pathologically enlarged mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymph nodes are
present.  No ascites, free air, or abdominal wall hernia.

CT PELVIS:

The bladder, prostate, and seminal vesicles are unremarkable.  The penile
prosthesis is unchanged in appearance with a collapsed reservoir demonstrated
within the left inguinal region.  No pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  No
free pelvic fluid.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:

Degenerative changes are stable.  No focal lytic or blastic lesion suspicious
for malignancy.  No evidence of discitis in this immunosuppressed patient.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No intraabdominal fluid collection to suggest abscess.

2.  Unchanged position of biliary stent with associated stable pneumobilia.

3.  Unchanged appearance of penile prosthesis with collapsed reservoir in left
inguinal region.

HISTORY:  A ___ man status post liver transplant on ___, hernia
repair one month ago, penile implant, status post prostatectomy ___ years ago
with Gram-negative rod bacteremia, query abscess or fluid collection.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted images were acquired on a 1.5
Tesla magnet including dynamic 3D imaging obtained prior to, during, and after
the uneventful intravenous administration of 0.1 mmol/kg (40 mL) of ProHance.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis of ___.

FINDINGS:

The patient has had a prior liver transplant.  There are multiple geographic
areas of subtly increased signal intensity on T2-weighted images in segment
VII and VIII (4:27, 34, 18).  Two of these lesions are only seen on the
T2-weighted images.  The lesion anteriorly in segment VIII (1301:36) does
demonstrate some arterial hyperenhancement compared to background liver
parenchyma.  In addition, the lesion in segment VII appears to contain
branching structures on the precontrast VIBE sequence (11:35).  In the
appropriate clinical conditions, these appearances could reflect changes
related to acute cholangitis.  

The spleen is not enlarged; however, it is low in signal intensity on
T2-weighted images and demonstrates loss of signal on in-phase compared to
out-of-phase T1-weighted images, consistent with siderosis.  The liver has a
similar pattern of signal loss on in-phase compared to the out-of-phase
T1-weighted images, although appearing subtle.  The portal vein and hepatic
veins are patent.  The hepatic arterial anastomosis is patent and appears to
be normal in caliber.  Mild intrahepatic duct dilatation with pneumobilia. 
There are multiple stents in the common bile duct, with suggesting of a
thickened duct wall.  The pancreas is atrophic and there are multiple cysts in
the body and tail of the pancreas. The largest is a 1.3-cm cyst in the
pancreatic body (5:11).  No peripancreatic edema.  No significant upper
abdominal lymphadenopathy. Both adrenal glands and both kidneys are
unremarkable in appearance except to note small simple cysts bilaterally.  No
free fluid.  The visualized osseous structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Three focal areas of signal abnormality in the right lobe of the liver
with relative T2 hyperintensity suggestive of but not diagnostic for
cholangitis.  No evidence of abscess.  Correlation with the patient's clinical
condition is advised.

2.  Siderosis in spleen and to a lesser extent in the liver.

3.  Mild intrahepatic duct dilatation, multiple biliary stents in situ.  CBD
wall appears somewhat ___ be reactive given the multiple stents, or
related to inflammation/infection.

4.  Multiple pancreatic cysts measuring up to 1.3 cm.  Given the patient's age
and the size of these lesions, recommend followup with noncontrast MRCP in one
year to ensure stability.

5.  Small right renal cysts.

TECHNIQUE:  A single frontal chest was reviewed in comparison with prior chest
radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS:

Patient has received a new left PICC line which ends just above the cavoatrial
junction.  There is no pleural abnormality. Both Lungs are clear.  Heart size,
mediastinal and hilar contours are normal.

IMPRESSION:  New left PICC line ends just above the cavoatrial junction.
